population.definition: Population of the municipality/city proper of Rabat (commune urbaine de Rabat) recorded in the 2024 general population and housing census (RGPH 2024, census date 1 September 2024) by the Haut-Commissariat au Plan (HCP) of Morocco, tabulated via citypopulation.de. The Rabat Prefecture counted 515,619 residents, while the twin city of Salé across the Bou Regreg estuary counted 945,101, forming an urban agglomeration of over 1.8 million people.

source.title: Morocco: Regions, Major Cities & Urban Communes (Census 2024)
source.publisher: CityPopulation (credits Haut-Commissariat au Plan, Royaume du Maroc)

facts.claim: Rabat was established in 1150 by the Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min as a ribat (fortified military camp) on a promontory overlooking the Atlantic and the Bou Regreg estuary.

source.title: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
source.quote: established in 1150 by the Almohad Caliph Abd al-Mu'min

facts.claim: In 1195 Caliph Abu Yaqub Yusuf al-Mansur planned to make Rabat the grand imperial capital of the Almohad empire (Ribat al-Fath), constructing monumental ramparts, gates and the Hassan Mosque.

source.title: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
source.quote: planned by Abu Yaqub Yusuf al-Mansur at the end of the 12th century

facts.claim: In 1912 General Hubert Lyautey chose Rabat as the administrative capital of the French Protectorate in Morocco, leading to urban planning that respected the historical city while adding the modern Ville Nouvelle.

source.title: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
source.quote: the new town was one of the largest and most ambitious modern urban projects in Africa in the 20th century

facts.claim: King Mohammed V reaffirmed Rabat as the national capital upon Morocco's recovery of independence in March 1956.

source.title: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
source.quote: retained as the capital of independent Morocco in 1956

facts.claim: In 2012 UNESCO inscribed Rabat on the World Heritage List as a shared heritage bridging ancient, medieval Islamic and 20th-century urban design.

source.title: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City: a Shared Heritage
source.quote: inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2012

places.what: A 12th-century Almohad citadel situated on a cliff over the Atlantic Ocean and the mouth of the Bou Regreg. It features the monumental Bab Oudaia gate, traditional blue-and-white residential alleys, an Andalusian garden and the historic Café Maure.

places.what: A historic complex combining the 44-metre incomplete Almohad minaret begun in 1195 and the 1971 royal mausoleum designed by Vietnamese-French architect Eric Vo Toan in Italian white marble, cedar and traditional zellij.

places.name: Musée Mohammed VI d'Art Moderne et Contemporain
places.what: The flagship national museum of modern and contemporary art in Morocco, opened in 2014 in central Rabat. Designed by architect Karim Chakor, it combines neo-Moorish architectural motifs with contemporary galleries showcasing Moroccan and international 20th- and 21st-century visual art.
